title: Complex analysis
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the analysis of functions of a complex variable: complex numbers and the Riemann sphere, analytic functions and the Cauchy–Riemann equations, power series and the elementary functions, contour integrals, Cauchy's theorem and integral formula, Liouville's theorem and the fundamental theorem of algebra, Taylor and Laurent series, singularities and residues, evaluation of real integrals, the argument principle and Rouché's theorem, and conformal maps.
primary_reading: A First Course in Complex Analysis by Beck, Marchesi, Pixton and Sabalka (free online)

weeks.1: Complex numbers, the plane and the Riemann sphere
weeks.2: Functions of a complex variable, limits and continuity
weeks.4: Power series, the exponential, logarithms and branches
weeks.5: Contour integrals and the estimation lemma
weeks.6: Cauchy's theorem and Cauchy's integral formula
weeks.7: Liouville's theorem, the maximum modulus principle and the fundamental theorem of algebra
weeks.9: Isolated singularities and the residue theorem
weeks.10: Evaluating real integrals and series with residues
weeks.11: The argument principle and Rouché's theorem

blocks.deliverable: Describe the images of supplied regions under simple maps.
Decide where supplied functions are analytic and choose a branch of the logarithm.
Evaluate contour integrals with Cauchy's integral formula.
Week 7 midterm; find Laurent series in supplied annuli.
Evaluate three real integrals with residues.
Count the zeros in a disk with Rouché's theorem and map a half-plane onto the disk.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Residue and mapping workbook: evaluate eight real integrals and two infinite series by residues with every contour justified, check each value numerically in plain Python, prove the fundamental theorem of algebra two ways (with Liouville's theorem and with Rouché's theorem), and construct and check three conformal maps between standard regions.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
